mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC (from -22.4% to -13.3%) indicates recovery momentum in consumer mobility. This trend continues linearly over the next four weeks, producing net positive direction in RETAIL_REC relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 9.1 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC four-week mean falls below -13.3% or declines week-on-week in three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility recovery (from -17.0% to -11.3%) drives commuting resumption, which increases incidental retail visits during work-week transit corridors. Each 1% rise in WORKPLACES produces 0.8% rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by >3 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES stalls or declines in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of WORKPLACES improvement.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed (-26.6%) relative to pre-pandemic baseline. Persistent transit avoidance constrains retail access for non-car-dependent populations, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth despite workplace recovery. RETAIL_REC cannot exceed -8% until TRANSIT recovers above -20%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -8% while TRANSIT remains below -20%, or TRANSIT recovers above -15% without corresponding RETAIL_REC acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows strong recovery trend (from -14.4% to +5.6%), indicating outdoor activity substitution and weekend leisure resumption. This behavioral shift toward outdoor recreation competes with indoor retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth to below -10% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds +3% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 20 percentage points over four weeks to +5.6%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while PARKS remains above +3%, or PARKS declines below 0% without RETAIL_REC acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility decline (from +9.0% to +5.1%) signals reduced home-confinement behavior. Combined with WORKPLACES recovery and TRANSIT persistence below -26%, consumers shift to car-based retail trips. RETAIL_REC rises +6 to +8 percentage points as car-dependent shopping increases.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +6% AND WORKPLACES improves above -12%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stabilizes above +6% or WORKPLACES stalls, and RETAIL_REC fails to rise by >4 percentage points within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM stability at +9% (unchanged over four weeks) indicates sustained essential-goods demand without volatility. This signals absence of new restrictions. Under no-restriction regime, RETAIL_REC continues recovery trajectory, reaching -8% to -5% over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at +9.1% mean over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM drops below +7% or spikes above +11%, signaling policy shift, and RETAIL_REC fails to improve by >4 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: February-to-March transition in Melbourne (late summer to autumn) produces seasonal shift in outdoor activity preference. PARKS recovery (+5.6%) combined with declining RESIDENTIAL confinement creates substitution effect: consumers allocate leisure time to parks over indoor retail, capping RETAIL_REC improvement at -12% or below.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while PARKS remains above +4% and RESIDENTIAL below +6%, or PARKS declines below +2% without RETAIL_REC acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT co-movement indicates commuting infrastructure constraint. TRANSIT at -26.6% severely lags WORKPLACES recovery at -11.3%, creating 15.3-point gap. This gap signals incomplete commuting recovery; RETAIL_REC cannot exceed -10% until TRANSIT-WORKPLACES gap narrows below 8 points.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -11.3% vs TRANSIT at -26.6%, gap of 15.3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while WORKPLACES-TRANSIT gap remains above 10 points, or gap narrows below 8 points without RETAIL_REC acceleration above -10%.
